reasoning: This was a Phase I dose-escalation study that successfully met its primary endpoint of establishing the MTD of pembrolizumab at 200 mg when combined with azacitidine. Step 1 (Target Engagement): While direct target engagement data is not provided, the established MTD suggests the combination was deliverable at therapeutic doses. Step 2 (Pathway Modulation): No biomarker data provided to assess pathway modulation. Step 3 (Clinical Translation): The study showed promising efficacy signals with 5/40 (12.5%) CR/CRi in R/R AML and 13/27 (48%) CR/CRi in newly diagnosed older patients, which are encouraging response rates for these difficult-to-treat populations. Step 4 (Population Effects): Clear differential response between cohorts, with newly diagnosed older patients showing much higher response rates (48% vs 12.5%). Step 5 (Confounders): This was appropriately designed as a Phase I study focused on safety and dose-finding, with efficacy as secondary endpoint.
